title: Kernel shift sync — shadow prefill & microbatch anomalies
summary: Weekly ops sync focused on shadow-cache prefill regressions observed in canary 12/02. We triaged microbatch jitter, kernel handshake time increases, and outlined short-term mitigations plus experimental knobs to test next sprint.
content:
Context:
- Canary deployment (canary-12) rolled kernel patch that changed handshake backoff. Started seeing a ~1.8-2.5ms median increase in kernel-handshake path for cold prompts during 12/02 canary run.
- At the same time, shadow prefill hit higher miss rate on sparse prompts (templates with long static prefixes) causing microbatch size to shrink and jitter token latency to increase.

Observed signals and quick metrics (canary-12, rolling window 12/02 00:00-18:00):
- Kernel handshake p50 increased from 0.9ms -> 2.6ms on cold path (samples where kv-cache miss + handshake executed).
- Microbatch average size dropped from 6.3 -> 4.1 for affected prompt class; 95th percentile token latency +22%.
- Shadow cache miss-rate for prefix-heavy templates: 14% -> 31% on canary nodes.
- No affect on hot-path steady-state; tail errors unchanged.

Immediate hypotheses discussed:
1) Kernel handshake backoff change introduced an extra scheduling point that races with prefill warmup, increasing latency when prefill hasn't completed.
2) Shadow cache indexing change (recent prefill merge) mis-aligns prefix hashing for some templated prompts -> higher miss-rate and extra cold-token work.
3) Microbatch generator has a thresholding bug that reduces batching when prefill latency spikes briefly (debounce too aggressive).
4) GC/allocator pauses on a subset of instances (older CUDA drivers) causing transient slowdown seen as jitter.

Experiments and tests run during the sync:
- Replayed canary traces in staging with kernel handshake reverted -> handshake p50 returned to ~0.95ms. Suggests kernel change is contributing.
- Added additional logging to prefill path to capture prefix-hash values and prefill timings for 1% traffic; found ~20% of the high-miss cases had mismatched hash prefixes due to string normalization regression.
- Disabled microbatch debounce in a small staging pool -> microbatch size recovered, but token latency variance increased slightly.
- Nighttime thermal logs checked: no consistent GC/driver pause aligned with observed spikes.

Decisions made in meeting:
- Rollback kernel handshake change in canary-12 while we root-cause. Migration notes: use revert PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/2184, coordinate with release-engineering.
- Hotfix prefill string normalization to align shadow cache hashing with production canonicalization; this is low-risk and should be pushed to canary within 24h.
- Re-enable microbatch debounce only after prefill miss-rate returns to <10% for 48h.

Short-term mitigations (next 72h):
- Rollback handshake change to canary nodes (owner: Miguel Torres, due: 2028-12-04).
- Apply normalization hotfix to shadow prefill (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2028-12-04).
- Increase sampling of prefill logs from 1% -> 5% for deeper telemetry (owner: Ethan Brooks, due: 2028-12-05).
- Add a synthetic workload that exercises templated long-prefix prompts in CI nightly (owner: Priya Shah, due: 2028-12-07).

Longer-term action items and investigations:
- Kernel handshake perf regression: add microbenchmark suite that isolates handshake and scheduling interactions; target: sprint 2 (owner: Miguel Torres).
- Microbatch generator robustness: audit debounce and threshold logic; consider adaptive debounce governed by observed prefill latency (owner: Ethan Brooks).
- Shadow cache eviction policy: validate that prefix-heavy templates don't thrash due to suboptimal TTLs; propose TTL tuning experiment (owner: Aisha Patel).
- Investigate possible driver/allocator interactions across heterogeneous fleets; correlate driver versions with spike incidents (owner: Lina Gomez, SRE).

Open questions and unresolved items:
- Why only certain templated prompts see hash mismatch? Early logs point to an upstream normalization change in text preprocessor; need to trace the change set diff.
- Is the microbatch debounce threshold appropriate for bursty workloads (e.g., query bursts with many cold sessions)? Need load modeling.
- Should we prefer prefill optimistic warming (speculative prefetch) vs conservative warming (wait for canonicalization) for these long-prefix templates? Tradeoff doc needed.

Notes from the triage runbook (raw, unpolished):
- If canary rollback shows handshake p50 back to baseline and prefill miss-rate drops after normalization fix -> proceed to promote handshake revert + prefill fix to production via staged rollout.
- If normalization fix does not reduce miss-rate below 12% within 48h, re-open hypothesis for possible index corruption and escalate to applied-ml for deeper model/tokenization review.

Meeting readouts and who to update:
- Notify release-engineering and schedule a brief handoff for the revert (Miguel).
- Post a condensed incident note in #serving-runtime with top-line metrics and mitigation status (Priya).
- Sync with product-hosted-api if user-visible latency or error budget risk increases (Lina).

Appendix — rapid log excerpts (sanitized):
- sample_id: 20281202-103212 | prefix_hash_before: 0x9a3f | prefix_hash_after: 0x0000 | prefill_time_ms: 48 | outcome: miss
- sample_id: 20281202-104720 | kernel_handshake_ms: 2.4 | microbatch_size: 3 | token_latency_p95_ms: 129

Retrospective notes (for next weekly):
- Improve canary observability: add delta metrics showing prefill miss-rate by prompt-class and kernel handshake delta per-instance.
- Consider a canary stabilization window longer than 6 hours for kernel scheduling patches.

End-of-sync quick wins:
- Push normalization patch to canary (Aisha) -> monitor.
- Revert kernel handshake for canary until benchmark suite added (Miguel).
- Add nightly synthetic exercising templated long-prefix prompts to CI (Priya).

-- Priya
